title: 4.4 A 0.36nW/0.9V 32kHz Crystal Oscillator Using Analog Regulation for Cross-Current Avoidance
problem: Ultra-low-power 32 kHz crystal oscillators typically require supply voltages >0.5 V to minimize switching losses in inverter-based circuits; recent pulsed-injection techniques achieve lower power but require additional regulation circuitry that isn't included in energy budgets, and don't operate efficiently from standard battery supply voltages (0.9–2 V).
motivation: Timekeeping is a critical background task in IoT devices and requires always-on operation from limited battery capacity; eliminating external regulation and direct battery operation at standard voltages simplifies system integration.
method: The oscillator's sustaining amplifier (the circuit that maintains the crystal's oscillations) uses analog regulation—electronic control without a separate voltage regulator—to prevent cross-currents, which are unwanted currents that waste power in the inverter (the core switching circuit). Unlike typical designs that reduce power by lowering the supply voltage, this approach keeps losses low by controlling when the inverter switches, eliminating cross-currents during switching transitions. Because power loss suppression happens through timing control rather than voltage reduction, no separate regulation circuit is needed, allowing the oscillator to run directly from standard battery voltages between 0.9 and 2 volts.
key_novelty: This 32 kHz oscillator is the first to achieve below-0.5-nanowatt power consumption from a 0.9-volt battery supply using analog regulation—control of switching timing to prevent power-wasting cross-currents—without a separate voltage regulator.
contributions: Analog regulation technique for cross-current avoidance in low-voltage sustaining circuits
Direct operation from 0.9–2 V battery supply without external regulation
Ultra-low power (0.36 nW) achieving 10–100x improvement over prior pulsed-injection designs
Time-domain regulation eliminating voltage-domain switching losses
baselines: conventional Pierce driver with RC filters
limitations: Frequency accuracy and temperature stability not specified in abstract; crystal quality factor dependency not discussed.
primary_theme: Ultra-low-power 32 kHz crystal oscillator with analog regulation for battery-powered IoT
